newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Bearish sentiment seen dominating Japan mkt.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Bearish sentiment seen dominating Japan mkt.

text.p: Japan's rubber futures markets are expected to be dominated by a lingering bearish mood next week, with the focus on the spot contract expiry on Tuesday, Japanese traders said on Friday.

"We are watching to see if spot June on TOCOM (Tokyo Commodity Exchange) will expire below 120 yen (per kg). If that happens, the market could succumb to further selling pressure," an analyst at a commodity broker said.

Traders said the expiry price could be weighed down by market participants' reluctance to take deliveries due to concerns over the quality of ribbed smoked sheet grade three rubber (RSS3) to be offered for delivery.
TOCOM benchmark November rubber futures contract ended the morning session at 127.2 yen per kg on Friday, against Thursday's close of 128.6 yen.
Benchmark November on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 128.4 yen per kg in the second morning session, against Thursday's close of 128.6 yen.
Even if the spot contract expires at a relatively steady price, the market lacks bullish factors to revive trade, traders said.

"A dearth of trading incentives is the main reason for the sluggish activity in recent months," another commodity broker said. "TOCOM benchmark November could fall below 120 yen as the summer draws near," he said.
Adding to the bearish outlook is the approaching seasonal rise in rubber production, traders said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 113.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, down from 116.00 U.S. cents on June 13.

Although Japan's rubber inventories have declined as Japanese traders have refrained from buying supplies due to concerns over quality, traders expected rubber stocks to start growing again from around the end of July.
Traders said they had been withholding purchases because the quality of rubber tends to deteriorate towards the end of the production season in May.

Japan rubber stocks as of June 10 amounted to 33,703 tonnes, the lowest level since August last year, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan. The figures were down about seven percent from the end of May.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 143 yen per kg as of Friday, compared with 148 yen on June 13.
